papers.title: MEO: Mining Reliable Expert Signals for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Wireless Networks
papers.summary: The operation of next-generation wireless networks increasingly hinges on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize critical network decisions. Offline RL trains agents using accessible datasets and thus eliminates costly online interactions, rendering it particularly advantageous in dynamic wireless environments that demand low latency and high safety. However, its capability remains under-explored in wireless settings, where offline data are often limited and subject to partial observability. papers.summary: Random access (RA) is one of the most foundational medium access control (MAC) layer scheduling schemes for handling unpredictable data traffic from multiple terminals. While multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been explored to optimize RA-based wireless networks, its reliance on experience-driven, distributed policy learning incurs significant training overhead for each optimization task, limiting its feasibility in real-world applications. papers.summary: Interaction is one of the core abilities of humanoid robots. However, most existing frameworks focus on non-interactive whole-body control, which limits their practical applicability. In this work, we develop InterReal, a unified physics-based imitation learning framework for Real-world human-object Interaction (HOI) control. InterReal enables humanoid robots to track HOI reference motions, facilitating the learning of fine-grained interactive skills and their deployment in real-world settings. papers.title: Demo: Closed-Loop Sionna-Isaac Sim Co-Simulation Framework for Wireless-Aware Robot Navigation over ROS 2
papers.summary: A robot that offloads its control loop to the network carries the receiver with it, so link quality is decided by where it goes. papers.title: Distributed Collaborative Positioning through ISAC for GPS-Denied Robotic Swarms
papers.summary: Robotic swarms in GPS-denied environments require accurate position and velocity in real-time for all nodes, without external infrastructure or centralized control. Existing positioning approaches, including collaborative positioning, fail because of non-scalable (O(N2)) measurement overhead or centralized architectures that cannot keep pace with high-mobility swarms. We present DiCoP, a novel paradigm of Distributed Collaborative Positioning through asynchronous, multi-static ISAC. papers.title: Towards Agile and Active Scene Update for Embodied Space Exploration: A WiFi-Guided Approach
papers.summary: Timely scene updating is essential for embodied agents operating in dynamic indoor environments. While cameras and LiDAR are effective for high-fidelity reconstruction and verification, relying on them alone for long-term maintenance is costly, since robots must repeatedly revisit large areas to rediscover relatively sparse changes. This paper presents WiDR, a WiFi-guided framework for efficient and active scene updating. papers.summary: This paper investigates the Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) framework under individual penalty constraints to address resource allocation challenges in dynamic wireless networked environments. Unlike conventional RMAB models, our model allows each user (arm) to have distinct and stringent performance constraints, such as energy limits, activation limits, or age of information minimums, enabling the capture of diverse objectives including fairness and efficiency. papers.title: METRO: MAP-Enhanced Twin Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning-Based Coverage and Capacity Optimization
papers.summary: Few-shot coverage and capacity optimization (CCO) under a small adjustment budget is challenging: model-based methods suffer from simulator mismatch, while feedback-based methods are sample-starved. We address this challenge with a rollout-based policy-improvement framework. papers.summary: Adaptive urban traffic signal control must coordinate motorized traffic, public transport, cyclists, and pedestrians under heterogeneous and highly dynamic demand. papers.title: Ethics and trust in social robot adoption for tourism: insights from Albania
papers.summary: Purpose Social robots are beginning to interact with guests in hotels, restaurants and tourist attractions, yet little is known about how travellers in emerging markets perceive their ethical implications or decide whether to trust them. This study aims to explore how participants in Albania evaluate the ethics of social robots and how these evaluations shape trust and adoption intention in tourism.
